title: Great but with great flaws
body:
I feel really conflicted because on one side I find it really great to exercise from home, with a wide variety of options, and also with meditation included. 
On the other side its flaws really feel unjustifiable for such a huge company, especially considering these are things customers have complained about for years. 
The two main issues for me are the lack of “levels” (beginner, medium, experienced etc), as I often end up with workouts way beyond my current fitness or experience level, when being able to increase difficulty up step by step would be the most beneficial option. 
The other main flaw is the fact that there isn’t a “resume workout” function or a way to go back/forward in the exercise (if the app/internet crashes, if you missed something etc). 
Since people have been complaining for years and apple has done nothing to fix these pretty straight forward flaws, it just feels like one of those projects that apple has just stopped spending any time on beyond business as usual.
Overall I think it’s good as part of Apple One (which I got for other reasons), but not something that I would pay for on its own unless the issues get fixed.

title: Great Potential, But Needs Better Data Visualization
body:
The Apple Fitness app is undoubtedly great, and I appreciate how seamlessly it tracks all my activities. The integration with the Apple Watch is excellent, and it keeps all my fitness data in one place. However, compared to what other apps offer, it’s just slightly below par.

One key feature missing is a monthly or yearly recap of activities. Having a clear summary of my progress over time would be incredibly motivating. Additionally, the app could really benefit from visualizing recovery processes, which are essential for balanced fitness.

Another suggestion would be to introduce widgets, like a monthly walking or running distance tracker, that could display data directly on the phone. These widgets and visualizations would make it easier to grasp long-term progress at a glance.

Apple clearly has all the data; it’s just not being utilized to its fullest potential. As a loyal user who loves the Apple Watch, I’d urge the developers to put in the effort to make tracking and visualizing fitness data more insightful and engaging.

title: Shockingly bad at calibrating distance.
body:
So I’ve been using this app to track my distance and calories burned for over a year now, but it wasn’t until I started training for a half marathon that I noticed that the distance the app says I’ve run was all over the place. There would be times I went ran the exact same distance two days apart but the app would say that one day I had ran an extra half a mile. 
 I knew it was inaccurate but I didn’t realise by how much until I ran the half marathon today. According to this fitness app, rather than running the standard 13.1 miles, the organisers must have been way off because according to my phone I’ve run over 18 miles today on the half marathon course. Shockingly bad!
 Overall I would rate this fitness app as terribly poor and inaccurate, but I suppose you can at least use it to compare the distances and calories that it says you’re burning from one day to the next. I’ll still use it for this purpose, just to keep track of which days I’ve worked harder than others, but as far as keeping an accurate record of these details I wouldn’t trust the app on this phone as far as I could throw it (and the phone would still claim I’d not thrown it as far as I actually had, just to provide another blow to my ego).

title: So glitchy and under developed. Possibly the worst Apple product.
body:
Dear Apple, you have all, absolutely all, of the ingredients to make a wonderful suite of fitness products. Your watches have amazing capabilities, your health app provides amazing insights, your phones collect even more data, but your fitness app is deeply under developed, with poor functionality and it’s hyper glitchy. The premise is really clever, the execution is extremely (read EXTREMELY) poor.

Goal setting is really great and motivating, but if your ‘awards’ glitch out, you can do 90 days of exercise only to lose the award for 100 days when it sticks on progress. It makes you want to give up or throw your Apple Watch on the floor. Your meditation body tracking is so far behind every other tracking device it blows my mind. ‘Open your phone for more metrics’ means ‘open your phone and you’ll see exactly the same two metrics you can see on your watch’. 

It feels like Apple aren’t invested in this app in the slightest.

title: Update Required
body:
I’ve been using this app with the intention of sharing and comparing my data with friends and family, which seemed like a promising feature initially. However, the experience has been less than satisfactory due to a persistent issue where the data does not always display correctly for shared profiles. Despite both parties being able to see my data without any problems, there are times when their data appears as zero to me, which is clearly inaccurate.

I’ve taken the time to meticulously check all the relevant settings on both my end and the end of my friends and family to ensure that everything is configured correctly for sharing. Despite these efforts, the issue persists, leading me to believe that this is an inherent problem with the app itself rather than a misconfiguration on our part.

This inconsistency in data sharing significantly undermines the utility and enjoyment of the app, as one of its core features does not function reliably. It’s disappointing to encounter such a fundamental flaw in an otherwise useful application. I hope the developers will address this issue in a future update to provide a more reliable and enjoyable experience for all users looking to share and compare their data with others.

title: Good but could be so much better.
body:
Currently in the trial phase and really love the quality of the videos and interaction from the trainers.  There are many videos for each workout type which is great.  So choice is brilliant if you only have a certain amount if time for example.  

I am used to Insanity HIIT workouts and these are really good.  The  treadmill running are good too - would like too many more that don’t have inclines as not many people will have these types of machines.  Perhaps someone could say if you don’t have an incline increase speed by X for example. 

Where is think it needs improving is the warmup & down and stretching after a workout. Which is THE MOST IMPORTANT PART of a workout. These should be incorporated within the workout as part of the workout.  I am struggling to find a PROPER cool down and stretching session for my HIIT workouts. There is lots of leg action in the HIIT but barely any form of strecthing the hamstring, groin and thigh area.  So I have do to my own.  If you want inspiration watch a few of the Insanity workouts.  Would love to see  more attention to this part  - or do a dedicated  Cool-down and stretch session which people can go to do as part of any exercise.  We could all do with the bit of extra stretching from time to time. 

I really like the way the instructors pass out the instructions.  What I would really like is to have the option to turn off the music though. I like to listen to certain music when exercising. Again something I think shouldn’t be that hard.  

Appreciate that this is relatively new and a work in progress.  Look forward to seeing more developments and enhancements.

title: Partly great but some obvious gaps
body:
I love some things about this service:

The sessions are fun and engaging. I have tried lots of rowing, core and some dancing.
The AirPlay on the TV works well apart from the occasional glitch.
It has been fun to do with the family - core and dancing anyway.

The specific feature I have found most irritating to date is that I can’t use my wife’s iPad to play rowing sessions.

More generally for a service that obtains a huge amount of data there is a weirdly ‘one size fits all’ approach to delivering the service. I would like to do a heavy weights session one day and recover the next. Do a hard run and be expected to take it easy for a few days. In my late 40s I would expect to be given more recovery time than I needed in my 20s. I would like a series of sessions - particularly on the rowing - which look at improving my VO2 max.

The stuff above seems tantalisingly possible.

One final thing - it may never rain in Southern California but for those of US who run in drizzle quite a lot a watch with a touch screen isn’t great. Some clarity on how to customise the buttons would be helpful.

title: Inadequate if pretty
body:
I’m still on the free version. I will not pay for it - any number of other workout programs do better if you’re travelling, not a gym member, or can’t afford equipment. 

Four things would greatly improve this app:

1. MORE BODYWEIGHT - you shouldn’t have to own gym equipment or pay for a gym membership to use this app. This is too expensive to be making you pay for extra things in order to use it fully.

2. An option to turn off the music. Many apps have this. You should too.

3. Better integration with other fitness app. If Apple sells the workouts, it should integrate with this in-system app.

4. The subtitles make it hard to see floor exercises. Generally, you need more attention to the technique details - foot placement, angle of bend, profile shots etc, but the fact that your own subtitles hide the positions the trainer is in is particularly poor design.

title: Housework Workouts
body:
Apple has the power to make some chores not only more entertaining, but more inclusive. I was doing some general cleaning in my house and was wondering if maybe I can select hoovering as a workout. I can’t now, but hopefully in the future Apple will make it available. 

We already know from research done with hotel housekeepers that when they were told their work is part of a healthy lifestyle, not only did they lose weight but also enjoyed what they were doing more, which in turn resulted in an increased feeling of well-being. 

Imagine your gym freak friend leaving your house a mess after a hang out. You can suggest that dish washing will burn a few calories and let them get going. Or your partner putting off some gardening because… reasons. If you’ve ever mowed the lawn or pulled weeds you know how demanding it is. 

Think of busy people who sometimes don’t have time to exercise but look after full-of-energy children or clean the house of a sick parent. This is exercise. Ticking these exercise and movements goals is reinforcing and builds momentum. 

Not to mention convincing more men that housework and raising children is also good for their health. This will help a lot of households, in my opinion. 

🤞🤞

There are people of all ages, shapes and nationalities. I like how it encourages me to finish a training with a cooldown that includes a meditation. I’d really like to see a series for women with pelvic floor exercises and other tailored work.  Minor irritants are the excessive (not sincere) smiling/happiness. But my bigger gripe is with the search function. It’s not well designed to help you find a workout: which Pilates works on your back - yoga balancing poses vs slow flows vs mat work - dance choreography vs dance exercises - which strength workout works your arms - which mindful cooldown works the part of your body you just worked on … etc And re the Rings: the targets are not easy to tailor. body:

Integration with the Watch is ok. I don’t see how having the rings displayed on the screen suddenly transforms your workout when it’s literally on your wrist. 

It’s also incredibly stereotypically AMERICAN. Everything is AWESOME to the MAX. I’m a fat cynical Irishman who feels no connection to some toned hunk/babe telling me to dig deep within myself for the final hill.

That said, the trainers are very pleasant with lots of perfectly toothy smiles and singing/rapping along with the music. This may or may not be a plus - I find it utterly irritating sometimes, but tolerable other times. Often, I wish I could just play my own music in the background. 

All in all, for the price, it’s decent enough - depending on what equipment you have at home, it’s a fraction of the cost of a gym membership. I wouldn’t buy an Apple Watch to use it - I like the Watch as a bit of tech, but making it an essential item overstretches the part it plays.

title: Avoid if looking for yoga content
body:

It feels very obnoxious and like it caters exclusively to a cliché parody of Californians.

It considers “yoga” to be one single amorphous thing, high-intensity flows performed by overenthusiastic Americans in overdecorated studios to Gen Z music (no wonder given Apple Music’s obsession with the same niche I suppose). No labelling or way of filtering by type of practice (there are a tremendously diverse set of kinds of yoga) or any useful descriptions of individual sessions (only a marketing preview for each video).

I’ve tried a lot of yoga apps on the App Store, and honestly, not a single one is worse than this. Maybe the other kinds of workout are better?

body:
Has anyone at Apple looked outside of West Coast America / the US and asked for feedback ? …… from a wide demographic of nationality and age ?

Do you think we want our spin classes to look like this ?

But flick through the previews…every preview is an instructor yelling (literally) at how they are gonna smash you to smithereens.  It’s like they have just been electrocuted.   Rather than have every workout at 200% intensity… why not have a bit of variety there.   For spinning for instance you can have more stamina oriented, you can incorporate dumbbells and upper body…and so on.

Apple Fitness is a great concept but it needs a lot more insightful thought from the content creators
